title: Spring Vegetable Fonio Pilaf
author: Pierre Thiam
desc: Shallot, garlic and carrot stewed in a half cup of broth, peas and corn folded in, then two cups of cooked fonio and scallions — the pilaf Thiam serves with his lamb shank mafé.
longDesc: The grain on the side of the plate in Thiam’s book. A shallot cooks about a minute until soft but not brown, garlic and a diced carrot cook three minutes more, a half cup of broth simmers the carrot about ten minutes under a lid, peas and corn go in for a minute, and two cups of already-cooked fonio and thin-sliced scallions are folded through. It is served hot or at room temperature, and it is the accompaniment named in the mafé and yassa entries (SEN021, SEN013).
ingredients: 1/4 cup fresh or frozen green peas
1/4 cup fresh or frozen corn kernels
Salt and freshly ground black pepper — quantities not printed
steps: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium-high. Cook the shallot about 1 minute, until soft but not brown.
Add the garlic and carrot and cook 3 more minutes, until the garlic is fragrant.
Add the broth, cover and simmer about 10 minutes, until the carrot is tender.
Add the peas and corn and cook about 1 minute.
Fold in the cooked fonio and the scallions. Season to taste. Serve hot or at room temperature.
chefTips: ‘Soft but not brown’ for the shallot, ‘fragrant’ for the garlic and ‘tender’ for the carrot are the three printed cues.
Cook the fonio first and let it cool slightly; it folds in more cleanly and doesn’t clump.
It is equally good at room temperature, as the page says.
commonMistakes: Stirring hard after the fonio goes in and breaking the grains.
reheating: A splash of water in a covered pan, or serve cool.
healthBenefits: Fonio is gluten-free and rich in amino acids methionine and cysteine.
Carrots, peas and corn give fibre and carotenoids.
culturalNote: Fonio is the ancient West African millet that Thiam has spent years bringing to markets; Saveur’s John O’Connor calls it ‘an ancient species of millet that was a staple before the French arrived’, making a comeback in the Casamance.
sources: Source as printed: Pierre Thiam, ‘The Fonio Cookbook’ (Lake Isle Press, 2019) — a different book from the two recipes beside it on the same Lake Isle page. Yield: ‘Serves 4’. TWO-PASS, agreement.
Cues in short fragments: shallot ‘soft but not brown’; garlic ‘fragrant’; carrots ‘tender’. Printing oddity: ‘1/4  cup’ for both peas and corn contains a double space.
ABSENT, not estimated: salt and pepper quantities.
